text:
tara: Alert from compliance: a handful of DB snapshot blobs in prod-bucket show no SSE header. Possible unencrypted-at-rest uploads. Not a drill. :eyes:

sec-bot: :rotating_light: DETECTED: OBJECT_NO_SSE - s3://prod-backups/db-snapshots/2026-04-02/ - 7 objects flagged. Ticket SEC-20260402-11

kevin: which uploader role wrote those objects?

ops-bot: audit hint: recent terraform apply changed iam role snapshot-uploader-prod to remove kms:Encrypt on the service role (PR #5222). Apply at 01:12 UTC.

anita: omg, that means the uploader couldn't call KMS to envelope encrypt, so it fell back to client-side plain upload? Need to confirm app behavior.

bob: checking service logs for upload errors around 01:12. grep: 
```
2026-04-02T01:12:08Z ERROR backup-uploader - kms:Encrypt AccessDenied for key arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456:key/cc33dd44 - falling back to direct putObject
```

bob: yep, fallback path exists for legacy reasons. It should have been removed.

tara: immediate actions: 1) revert TF change to restore kms:Encrypt permission, 2) quarantine the 7 objects (move to isolated bucket), 3) rotate the CMK and re-encrypt copies from cold snapshots, 4) notify compliance. Anyone object?

kevin: Revert will be quick. But rotating a CMK will break existing encrypted snapshots unless we rewrap data keys. Suggest: create a new CMK and use it for re-encrypt job; do not schedule destructive rekey yet.

anita: I'll run a scan for uploads that hit the fallback path between 01:10-01:20 and list objects. CLI I used: 
```
index=uploads event=PutObject AND message="falling back to direct putObject" | stats count by s3.key
```

anita: found 23 objects across two prefixes, not just DB snapshots. Some may be customer backups.

bob: quarantine in progress: copying flagged objects to s3://incident-quarantine/2934567890/ with --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id cc33dd44-new. Throttling to avoid KMS rate limits.

kevin: Reverted TF in repo, running apply now. Also adding a pre-apply validator to block removing kms:Encrypt from any uploader role. PR protection + manual review required.

tara: good. Postmortem items: remove fallback path from uploader binary, add unit test to prevent fallback, tighten RBAC change reviews, add alert that flags any PutObject with no ServerSideEncryption header.

anita: I'll draft compliance notification and gather object list + timestamps. We'll confirm whether any plaintext exfil occurred by checking access logs (GETs) for those objects.

ops-bot: Created incident channel #incident-2934567890, incident id INC-20260402-74.

tara: thanks. Keep updates in the incident channel. If we confirm customer data was written unencrypted, we need coordinated customer comms and legal loop-in.

(ends)
